Fallback contract implemented — 1 of 8 constructs round-tripped before, 8 of 8 now

Operator ruled unwrap on the open question, so all four decisions are settled and the contract is built. GitHub PR 63 off master, branch fix-63-lossy-fallback-contract, three commits. Not merged and not deployed — see the end.

The headline, measured

The eight shapes pinned before any change, through tw -> md -> tw:

measurebeforeafter
round-trips byte-for-byte1 of 88 of 8

The one that round-tripped before was {{{#!comment}}}, and comment 12's finding is why that was the worst of the eight rather than the best: byte-identical and semantically inverted. It is now carried verbatim and warned.

What landed

  1. The pin, before touching anything. Three classes with different jobs — 11 constructs that must keep round-tripping (the recall gate), 2 that normalise, 8 characterised as broken. Watched failing on four seeded defects per ​auto_pm:wiki:Rules/testing/SeededDefectFirst.
  2. The fallback and the unwrap. Read leg emits the original source verbatim in a tracwiki-unconverted fence; write leg unwraps it. Three defects surfaced while building it, each caught by a test that already existed rather than by inspection: the fallback runs before the converter's own shielding and needed its own, adjacent fallback blocks ran their fences together into a malformed run, and the table warnings still described the reconstruction that had been removed.
  3. The deletion. _convert_processor_cells, 39 lines.

One choice I made that you did not rule on

The fence tag is tracwiki-unconverted, not a bare tracwiki. The tag is what the write leg unwraps on, so a collision with a code sample someone wrote while documenting TracWiki inside a Markdown file would inject live markup where a code block was meant — the exact class of corruption this ticket removes. Say the word if you want it spelled differently.

The near-miss, because it is the ticket's own trap firing

Making _convert_processor_cells a no-op left 1537 tests passing — which reads as "unreachable, safe to delete." Measured directly instead of inferred from the green suite, it was neither unreachable nor safe:

sourceafter conversion
a plain code block whose body is a #!td processor cella fenced block whose body is ||a|| — the quoted source rewritten

It ran before the code-block stashing, so a processor cell nested inside a plain code block was rewritten too. The #31 / #51 family, and nothing in the suite covered it. This ticket's acceptance section warns that "tests still pass" is satisfied by deleting the code under test; here it was equally satisfied by not deleting it. The test was written and watched failing first, so the deletion is a bug fix and not only a simplification.

The line count went up. Comment 3, comment 6 and comment 7 each predicted the "large chunks" premise would not hold, and it did not; you have already ruled that the drop need not match the expectation, so this is recorded rather than argued.

Deliberately not in this PR

  • Definition lists, the fifth broken construct. Its detector is far too broad to hand a fallback to — measured, Use std::vector here. already converts to **Use std**: vector here., so wrapping on that signal would put ordinary prose inside a code fence. That over-broad detector is a live pre-existing defect and wants its own ticket; I have not filed it yet.
  • #68's write-leg loss check — separate ticket, separate PR, still the write half of the contract.
  • A second pre-existing weakness found while deleting: a #!lang block nested directly inside another #!lang block produces malformed intermediate Markdown and gains a blank line before the outer close. Measured on master for every nested block, so it predates this. On master that shape was corrupted instead, so this is strictly better, but it is not clean.

One decision I need before step 5

The write-leg fallback has no obvious wrapping unit, and I did not want to invent one. The read leg's unit is self-evident — the block construct. A Markdown footnote is not a block: the reference [^1] and its definition [^1]: note sit in different places in the document, and wrapping either alone breaks the pairing. Measured, the converter does not parse footnotes at all — only the table plugin is enabled, so the definition line is consumed as a link reference definition and Text[^1] is stored as Text[wiki:note ^1], a fabricated link to a page named note.

Three options, none obviously right:

  1. wrap the whole document in {{{#!markdown}}} when any unrepresentable construct is present — safe, drastic;
  2. wrap the enclosing block of each half separately and accept the broken pairing;
  3. fail the call for this narrow class only, which is comment 1's original write-leg proposal surviving in exactly the place it fits.

I lean (c), narrowly scoped: it is the one construct class where wrapping genuinely cannot preserve meaning, and the author's escape hatch is real — declare format="tracwiki" and nothing converts.

Merge and deploy?

Same question as slice (b). PR 63 is up and unmerged; deploying restarts both shared units every project connects to, so it wants to be a deliberate call rather than a tail-end step.
